subject: chemistry
topicDisplay: Chemical formulae, equations and amount of substance
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the Eduqas spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE Eduqas Chemistry simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: What is the correct formula for aluminium oxide (Al3+ and O2-)?
questions.explain: To balance charges, two Al3+ (total +6) combine with three O2- (total -6), giving Al2O3.

questions.q: What is the formula for calcium nitrate, given the nitrate ion is NO3- and calcium is Ca2+?
questions.explain: One Ca2+ needs two NO3- ions to balance the charge, so the formula is Ca(NO3)2. Brackets show the whole nitrate ion is doubled.

questions.q: Balance: __ H2 + __ O2 -> __ H2O. The correct coefficients are:
questions.explain: 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O gives 4 H and 2 O on each side. Atoms are conserved.

questions.q: Balance: __ Na + __ Cl2 -> __ NaCl. The coefficients are:
questions.explain: 2Na + Cl2 -> 2NaCl balances 2 Na and 2 Cl on each side.

questions.q: Calculate the relative formula mass (Mr) of CO2 (C=12, O=16).
Calculate the Mr of calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (Ca=40, C=12, O=16).
One mole of any substance contains how many particles (the Avogadro constant)?
questions.explain: One mole contains 6.02 x 10 to the power 23 particles - the Avogadro constant.

questions.q: How many molecules are in 2 moles of water?
questions.explain: Number = moles x Avogadro constant = 2 x 6.02 x 10 to the 23 = 1.204 x 10 to the power 24 molecules.

questions.q: How many moles are in 88 g of CO2 (Mr = 44)?
questions.explain: Moles = mass / Mr = 88 / 44 = 2 mol.

questions.q: What is the mass of 0.25 mol of calcium carbonate, CaCO3 (Mr = 100)?
questions.explain: Mass = moles x Mr = 0.25 x 100 = 25 g.

questions.q: How many moles are in 20 g of sodium hydroxide, NaOH (Mr = 40)?
questions.explain: Moles = mass / Mr = 20 / 40 = 0.5 mol.

questions.q: In 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO, how many moles of MgO form from 0.5 mol of Mg?
questions.explain: The ratio of Mg to MgO is 2:2, i.e. 1:1, so 0.5 mol Mg gives 0.5 mol MgO.

questions.q: CaCO3 -> CaO + CO2. What mass of CaO (Mr = 56) forms from 100 g of CaCO3 (Mr = 100)?
questions.explain: 100 g CaCO3 = 1 mol. The 1:1 ratio gives 1 mol CaO. Mass = 1 x 56 = 56 g.

questions.q: What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in water, H2O (H=1, O=16, Mr=18)?
questions.explain: % O = (16 / 18) x 100 = 88.9%. The two H atoms make up the remaining 11.1%.

questions.q: Calculate the percentage by mass of nitrogen in nitrogen dioxide, NO2 (N=14, O=16, Mr=46).
A compound contains 0.2 mol Mg and 0.2 mol O. Its empirical formula is:
questions.explain: The mole ratio Mg:O is 0.2:0.2 = 1:1, so the empirical formula is MgO.

questions.q: A compound contains 0.4 mol iron and 0.6 mol oxygen. Its empirical formula is:
questions.explain: Ratio Fe:O = 0.4:0.6 = 2:3, so the empirical formula is Fe2O3.

questions.q: What is the concentration (in g/dm3) of a solution containing 20 g of solute in 0.5 dm3?
questions.explain: Concentration = mass / volume = 20 / 0.5 = 40 g/dm3.

questions.q: A reaction has a theoretical yield of 50 g but only 40 g is obtained. What is the percentage yield?
questions.explain: % yield = (actual / theoretical) x 100 = (40 / 50) x 100 = 80%.

questions.q: In a sealed flask, 10 g of reactant A reacts fully with 15 g of reactant B. What mass of products forms?
questions.explain: Mass is conserved: total product mass = 10 + 15 = 25 g. No atoms are created or destroyed.
